'''Gujarat International Finance Tec-City''' also called '''GIFT City''', is a central business district under construction in the [[Gandhinagar district]] as a suburb city of [[Gandhinagar]]-[[Ahmedabad]] Metropolitan Region in [[Gujarat]], India. It is India's first operational [[Greenfield land|greenfield]] [[smart city]] and international financial services centre, which the [[Government of Gujarat]] promoted as a [[greenfield project]]. In 2020 [[GIFT International Financial Services Centre|GIFT IFSC]] bagged 10th place in [[Global Financial Centres Index#Top 15 centres by industry sector|Finance Industry]] and top rank in emerging financial centres in the [[Global Financial Centres Index#Financial centre profiles|Global Financial Centres Index]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Reporter |first=B. S. |date=2017-10-03 |title=GIFT City's IFSC bags 10th place in Global Financial Centres Index |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/markets/gift-city-s-ifsc-bags-10th-place-in-global-financial-centres-index-117100200495_1.html |access-date=2023-03-22 |website=www.business-standard.com |language=en |archive-date=22 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230422043959/https://www.business-standard.com/article/markets/gift-city-s-ifsc-bags-10th-place-in-global-financial-centres-index-117100200495_1.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=S |first=Rajalakshmi |date=2017-10-02 |title=GIFT-IFSC ranks at 10th place in Global Financial Centres Index |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/markets/giftifsc-among-top-15-global-financial-centres/article9883732.ece |access-date=2023-03-22 |website=www.thehindubusinessline.com |language=en |archive-date=22 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230422050134/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/markets/giftifsc-among-top-15-global-financial-centres/article9883732.ece |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2025, GIFT City secured the top rank in reputational advantage, ranked 40th in fintech, and achieved an overall ranking of 46th in the Global Financial Centres Index (GFCI 37).<ref>{{Cite news |date=Mar 26, 2025 |title=GIFT City climbs global financial centre index, bolsters its hub status |url=https://www.business-standard.com/economy/news/gift-city-climbs-global-financial-centre-index-bolsters-its-hub-status-125032600948_1.html}}</ref>

The city is located on the banks of the [[Sabarmati River]] and is around {{cvt|12|km}} from [[Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport]].<ref name=":12">{{Cite web|url=http://www.gudcltd.com/gujarat-international-finance-tech-city|title=THE GUJARAT INTERNATIONAL FINANCE TEC-CITY (GIFT)|website=www.gudcltd.com|language=en|access-date=2018-02-02|archive-date=9 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190609031628/http://gudcltd.com/gujarat-international-finance-tech-city|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":10">{{cite web|url=http://www.businesstoday.in/sectors/infra/gift-city-gujarat-international-finance-tec-city-jobs-companies-offices/story/268278.html|title=GIFT makes steady progress; witnesses a 'hockey stick growth curve'|website=www.businesstoday.in|date=17 January 2018|access-date=1 November 2018|archive-date=25 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180625021957/https://www.businesstoday.in/sectors/infra/gift-city-gujarat-international-finance-tec-city-jobs-companies-offices/story/268278.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/more-gifts-for-gift-city-might-stop-flight-of-capital-to-singapore/articleshow/62744143.cms|title=More gifts for GIFT City may stop flight of capital to Singapore|last=Subramanian|first=N. Sundaresha|date=2018-02-01|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2018-02-02|archive-date=24 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180624211238/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/more-gifts-for-gift-city-might-stop-flight-of-capital-to-singapore/articleshow/62744143.cms|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":11">{{cite web |title= Developments of Gandhinagar|url= https://www.nationsroot.in/member/ahmedabad-west-mp-dr-kirit-p-solanki |access-date= 14 September 2018 |archive-date= 31 December 2019 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20191231110610/https://www.nationsroot.in/member/ahmedabad-west-mp-dr-kirit-p-solanki |url-status= dead }}</ref> The city is designed so residents can walk to work, and includes commercial, financial and residential complexes. The city is connected through 4–6 lane [[State highways in India|state]] and [[National highways of India|national]] highways. The area is also served by the GIFT City metro station, connecting GIFT City to the [[Ahmedabad Metro]] network.<ref>{{cite web | title=Direct metro links to Gandhinagar, GNLU & Gift City | url=https://infra.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/urban-transportation/direct-metro-links-to-gandhinagar-gnlu-gift-city/118273016 }}</ref> The total area for the development of GIFT is {{convert|886|acre|order=flip}} out of which the [[special economic zone]] (SEZ) constitutes {{convert|261|acre|order=flip}}. The project area under development can hence be classified under the SEZ area and the non-SEZ area (also known as the [[Domestic tariff area]] or the DTA).<ref name="Bloomberg 2022">{{cite news |last1=Rodrigues |first1=Jeanette |last2=Sircar |first2=Subhadip |title=India's Free-Market Oasis Aims to Take On Singapore and Dubai |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2022-11-29/which-city-will-be-next-singapore-or-dubai-new-india-finance-hub-has-big-plans |access-date=29 November 2022 |work=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=29 November 2022 |language=en |archive-date=29 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221129022329/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2022-11-29/which-city-will-be-next-singapore-or-dubai-new-india-finance-hub-has-big-plans |url-status=live }}</ref>

Leadership at GIFT City has also evolved with its expansion. In July 2025, Sanjay Kaul was appointed as the new managing director and Group CEO.

During the meeting with top management of HSBC Plc, [[Finance minister of india|FM]] [[Nirmala Sitharaman]] outlined the roadmap towards Viksit Bharat, towards [[Atmanirbhar Bharat]], sustainability, innovation, adoption of [[Artificial Intelligence (AI)]] and inclusivity. GIFT [[GIFT International Financial Services Centre|IFSC]], international financial services centre, is in [[Gandhinagar]] [[Gujarat]].

The [[Artificial intelligence (AI)|AI]] Centre of Excellence at GIFT City is aimed at creating a unified platform that brings together solution developers, experts, professionals, and start-ups under one roof, said [[Bhupendrabhai Patel|Shri Bhupendra Patel]] at the time of the launch of [[Infosys]] Development Centre at GIFT City.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Infosys Development Centre at GIFT City inaugurated |url=https://www.ahmedabadmirror.com/infosys-development-centre-at-gift-city-inaugurated/81892763.html |access-date=2025-12-03 |website=Ahmedabad Mirror |language=en}}</ref>

Several multinational banks including [[J.P. Morgan & Co.|JP Morgan]], [[Standard Chartered]], [[Deutsche Bank]], [[Citibank]], [[HSBC]]. [[Barclays Bank]], [[Bank of America]], [[DFCC Bank]], [[Qatar National Bank]] have set up IFSC Banking Units here.<ref>{{cite web | title=Gujarat: 8 international banks set up offices at GIFT City | work=The Times of India | date=28 May 2022 | url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/8-international-banks-set-up-offices-at-gift-city/articleshow/91844161.cms }}</ref>  Furthermore, it includes 35 fintech entities, two international stock exchanges with average daily trading volumes of $30.6 billion, as well as India's first [[India International Bullion Exchange|international bullion exchange]] with 75 onboarded jewellers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Why Google Chose Gujarat For Its Global Fintech Operations Hub |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/news/why-google-chose-gujarat-for-its-global-fintech-operations-hub/86119/1 |access-date=2023-06-29 |website=Forbes India |language=en |archive-date=29 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230629093421/https://www.forbesindia.com/article/news/why-google-chose-gujarat-for-its-global-fintech-operations-hub/86119/1 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Google To Set Up A Centre In GIFT City — Will This Boost The Fintech Ecosystem In India? |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/audio/to-the-point/google-to-set-up-a-centre-in-gift-city-will-this-boost-the-fintech-ecosystem-in-india/86133 |access-date=2023-06-26 |website=Forbes India |language=en |archive-date=26 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230626181448/https://www.forbesindia.com/audio/to-the-point/google-to-set-up-a-centre-in-gift-city-will-this-boost-the-fintech-ecosystem-in-india/86133 |url-status=live }}</ref> With the opening of the first campuses of two Australian universities on 7 November 2023 in the presence of Indian counterpart [[Dharmendra Pradhan]] and Australian Education Minister [[Jason Clare]], GIFT City is beginning to establish itself as the centre of foreign universities in the nation.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Langa |first=Mahesh |date=7 November 2023 |title=Two Australian Universities open in GIFT City |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/other-states/two-australian-universities-open-in-gift-city/article67504753.ece |access-date=7 November 2023}}</ref>

== Etymology ==
The name "GIFT" is an acronym that stands for "Gujarat International Finance Tec-City". The word "[[Gujarat]]" refers to the [[western India]]n state where the city is located. "[[International city|International]]" signifies that the city is intended to be a global hub for financial and business services, attracting businesses and investors from around the world. "Finance" highlights the primary focus of the development, which is to create a world-class financial centre."Tec-City" stands for "Technology-based SEZ" (Special Economic Zone).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gujarat International Finance Tec-City |url=https://gift-web-assets.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/RTI-08Aug2022.pdf |website=GIFT City |access-date=30 March 2023 |archive-date=5 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405101925/https://gift-web-assets.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/RTI-08Aug2022.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref>

==History==
[[File:Shri Sudhir Mankad, Chairman, GIFT City, presenting key of GIFT City to the Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, at the inauguration ceremony of the India International Exchange in GIFT City, Gandhinagar, Gujarat.jpg|thumb| Prime Minister [[Narendra Modi]] in 2017 at the [[India International Exchange]] inauguration ceremony in GIFT City.<ref name=":2">{{cite news|title=PM Modi to inaugurate 16-storey international exchange in Gujarat to rival Singapore, Dubai|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/pm-modi-to-inaugurate-16-storey-international-exchange-in-gujarat-to-rival-singapore-dubai/articleshow/56420183.cms|access-date=16 January 2017|agency=[[Indo-Asian News Service]]|publisher=India Times|date=9 January 2017|archive-date=11 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170111183454/http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/pm-modi-to-inaugurate-16-storey-international-exchange-in-gujarat-to-rival-singapore-dubai/articleshow/56420183.cms|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{cite news|title=PM Narendra Modi launches India's first international stock exchange|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/education-today/gk-current-affairs/story/modi-launches-india-stock-exchange-gift-city-954720-2017-01-13|access-date=16 January 2017|publisher=India Today|date=13 January 2017|archive-date=25 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211025072940/https://www.indiatoday.in/education-today/gk-current-affairs/story/modi-launches-india-stock-exchange-gift-city-954720-2017-01-13|url-status=live}}</ref>]]

On 15 December 2011, ''[[The Economic Times]]'' reported city officials in GIFT were inviting companies from Singapore that wished to expand but could not do so due to a lack of land in Singapore to open their businesses in GIFT. Investments from banks, private equity companies, insurance companies and asset management companies were considered.<ref name=":5">{{cite web |url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2011-12-15/news/30520461_1_singapore-firms-singapore-government-financial-sector |title=Singapore firms get Gujarat International Finance Tec City (GIFT) invite – The Economic Times |website=Articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com |date=2011-12-15 |access-date=2017-01-03 |archive-date=22 January 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120122014757/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2011-12-15/news/30520461_1_singapore-firms-singapore-government-financial-sector |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 26 December 2011, ''[[The Times of India]]'' reported China's technology giant [[Huawei]] was likely to provide technology to GIFT. According to Eric Yu, president, of enterprise business of [[Huawei|Huawei India]], this technology included networks, data centres and surveillance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/Chinas-Huawei-to-provide-tech-for-GIFT/articleshow/11126939.cms |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120116131308/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2011-12-16/ahmedabad/30524622_1_huawei-india-international-finance-tec-city-sis |url-status=live |archive-date=2012-01-16 |website=[[The Times of India]] |title= China's Huawei to provide tech for GIFT |date=16 December 2011 |access-date=2017-01-03}}</ref>

On 2 October 2014, NetIndian reported a new World Trade Centre would be set up in GIFT City as per an agreement between the World Trade Centre India Services Council (WTCS) and GIFT City Ltd. It would be completed within four years.<ref name=":6">{{cite web |url=http://netindian.in/news/2014/10/02/00030771/gift-city-gcci-world-trade-centre-pact-trade-development |title=GIFT City, GCCI and World Trade Centre in pact for trade development | NetIndian |website=Netindian.in |date=2014-10-02 |access-date=2017-01-03 |archive-date=8 November 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141108070916/http://netindian.in/news/2014/10/02/00030771/gift-city-gcci-world-trade-centre-pact-trade-development |url-status=live }}</ref>

BSE Broker's Forum planned to invest {{INRConvert|1.2|b|lk=r|year=2017}} to build a commercial tower to set up back-office operations. They were allocated {{convert|300000|sqft|m2|order=flip}} to develop the commercial tower with the likelihood of setting up an exchange office.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/money/report-bse-to-set-up-commercial-tower-at-gift-city-in-gujarat-2026420 |title=BSE to set up commercial tower at GIFT city in Gujarat | Latest News & Updates at Daily News & Analysis |website=Dnaindia.com |date=2014-10-15 |access-date=2017-01-03 |archive-date=18 November 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141118164007/http://www.dnaindia.com/money/report-bse-to-set-up-commercial-tower-at-gift-city-in-gujarat-2026420 |url-status=live }}</ref>

According to ''[[The Times of India]]'' on 18 October 2014, the [[Bangalore]]-based [[Brigade Group]] would invest {{INRConvert|5|b|year=2014}} over the next few years to develop {{convert|1.1|e6sqft|e6m2|abbr=off|order=flip}} of built-up area with a future option of investing another {{INRConvert|6|b|year=2014}} to develop {{convert|1.7|e6sqft|e6m2|order=flip}}.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/Brigade-Group-to-invest-Rs-500-crore-in-GIFT-City-as-co-developer/articleshow/44867808.cms |title=Brigade Group to invest Rs 500 crore in GIFT City as co-developer – Times of India |website=Timesofindia.indiatimes.com |date=2014-10-18 |access-date=2017-01-03 |archive-date=20 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020175522/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/Business/India-Business/Brigade-Group-to-invest-Rs-500-crore-in-GIFT-City-as-co-developer/articleshow/44867808.cms |url-status=live }}</ref>

In November 2018, [[The Wire (India)|The Wire]] reported the Government of Gujarat State would buy out the 50% stake of beleaguered [[Infrastructure Leasing & Financial Services]] (IL&FS) in the GIFT City to minimize delays to the project.<ref name=":7">{{cite web|url=https://thewire.in/political-economy/gujarat-buying-crisis-hit-ilfs-stake-gift-city-vijay-rupani|title=Gujarat Will Buy Crisis-Hit IL&FS Stake in 'Gift City', Says CM Vijay Rupani|website=The Wire|access-date=29 January 2019|archive-date=27 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181127114848/https://thewire.in/political-economy/gujarat-buying-crisis-hit-ilfs-stake-gift-city-vijay-rupani|url-status=live}}</ref> In June, 2020, IL&FS concluded sale of its stake in GIFT-City for {{INRConvert|320|m|year=2020}} equity value to the state government.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2020-06-08|title=IL&FS sells 50% stake in GIFT City to Gujarat govt, reduces consolidated debt by over Rs 1,200 crore|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/ilfs-sells-50-pc-stake-in-gift-city-to-gujarat-govt-reduces-consolidated-debt-by-over-rs-1200-crore/articleshow/76260582.cms|access-date=2020-06-09|archive-date=21 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200621050340/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/ilfs-sells-50-pc-stake-in-gift-city-to-gujarat-govt-reduces-consolidated-debt-by-over-rs-1200-crore/articleshow/76260582.cms|url-status=live}}</ref>

According to ''[[Business Standard]]'', OPS Fund Services, a subsidiary of OPS Global, Singapore, received a license to open in the International Financial Service Centre at GIFT city.<ref name=":8">{{cite web|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/boost-for-aif-biz-at-gift-city-as-top-fund-administrator-gets-license-119011400379_1.html|title=Boost for AIF biz at Gift city as top fund administrator gets license|first=Rajesh|last=Bhayani|date=14 January 2019|via=Business Standard|access-date=29 January 2019|archive-date=29 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190129181319/https://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/boost-for-aif-biz-at-gift-city-as-top-fund-administrator-gets-license-119011400379_1.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 5 December 2019, ''Business Standard'' reported that [[Bank of America]] opened a Global Business Services Center at GIFT.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/finance/bank-of-america-opens-global-business-services-center-at-gift-ifsc-119120601155_1.html|title=Bank of America opens Global Business Services Center at GIFT-IFSC|last=Umarji|first=Vinay|date=2019-12-06|work=Business Standard India|access-date=2020-01-23|archive-date=14 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114144851/https://www.business-standard.com/article/finance/bank-of-america-opens-global-business-services-center-at-gift-ifsc-119120601155_1.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 6 January 2020, [[Accor]] opened the first international hotel in GIFT City.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.traveldailymedia.com/accor-opens-the-first-international-hotel-in-gift-city/|title=Accor opens the first international hotel in GIFT City|date=2020-01-06|website=Travel Daily|language=en-US|access-date=2020-01-23|archive-date=15 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230215050734/https://www.traveldailymedia.com/accor-opens-the-first-international-hotel-in-gift-city/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 20 January 2020, [[The Economic Times]] reported GIFT was ready to begin trading in rupee-dollar in the [[futures market]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/forex/gift-city-to-begin-trading-in-rupee-dollar-in-futures-market/articleshow/73444484.cms|title=GIFT City to begin trading in rupee-dollar in futures market|last=Das|first=Saikat|date=2020-01-20|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2020-01-23|archive-date=10 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200710082602/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/forex/gift-city-to-begin-trading-in-rupee-dollar-in-futures-market/articleshow/73444484.cms|url-status=live}}</ref>

The total area for the development of GIFT is {{convert|886|acre|order=flip}} out of which the [[Special economic zone|SEZ]] (Special Economic Zone) constitutes {{convert|261|acre|order=flip}}. The project area under development can hence be classified under the [[Special economic zone|SEZ]] area and the non-SEZ area (also known as the Domestic Tariff area or the DTA).<ref>{{Cite web |title=GIFT City division |url=https://wtcgiftcity.org/attachments/project-update.pdf |website=wtcgiftcity.org |access-date=28 March 2023 |archive-date=28 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230328070204/https://wtcgiftcity.org/attachments/project-update.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=ShivaniDarji2 |date=2020-05-09 |title=Gift city Presentation |url=https://www.slideshare.net/ShivaniDarji2/gift-city-presentation-233487679 |access-date=28 March 2023 |archive-date=28 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230328070205/https://www.slideshare.net/ShivaniDarji2/gift-city-presentation-233487679 |url-status=live }}</ref>

As of June 2025, GIFT City had 939 registered entities. The hub currently houses 47 insurance firms and 272 funds, with more than 100 foreign companies, half of which joined in the last year.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-08-20 |title=GIFT IFSC set to cross 1k registrations, $100 billion assets |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/gift-ifsc-set-to-cross-1k-registrations-100-billion-assets/articleshow/123412949.cms |access-date=2025-12-03 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

GIFT City is divided into two zones:

# Domestic Tariff Area (DTA): This zone is meant for domestic companies and is subject to Indian laws and regulations. Companies operating within this zone can cater to the domestic market and benefit from various tax incentives offered by the Indian government.
# Special Economic Zone (SEZ): This zone is meant for international companies and is designed to promote exports and foreign investments. Companies operating within this zone enjoy a range of incentives, including tax exemptions, duty-free imports and exports, and simplified regulatory procedures.The SEZ has been further divided into two zones: SEZ PA (Processing Area) and SEZ NPA (Non-Processing Area).
##The SEZ PA is the core of the GIFT City and is designed to provide state-of-the-art infrastructure to various financial institutions, banks, and other businesses. The SEZ PA comprises commercial buildings, residential towers, a convention centre, and a recreational area. This zone is primarily intended for businesses that require specialized infrastructure, tax incentives, and other benefits provided by the SEZ Act.
##On the other hand, the SEZ NPA is the area surrounding the SEZ PA and is intended to provide support services to the businesses operating in the SEZ PA. It includes residential apartments, hotels, hospitals, schools, and other support facilities.

The city is divided into the following divisions by area:
* International Financial Services Centre (IFSC): This division is the main focus of GIFT City and is India's first IFSC. It is designed to cater to the financial services industry and provides a world-class business environment.
* Domestic Finance Centre (DFC): This division is designed to cater to the needs of the domestic financial services industry. It provides a platform for the growth of Indian financial services companies.
* Multi-services SEZ: This division is a Special Economic Zone (SEZ) that provides a platform for companies to set up their businesses in various sectors such as IT/ITES, engineering, biotechnology, and pharmaceuticals.
* Social and Civic Infrastructure: This division provides world-class social and civic infrastructure to the residents of GIFT City, including schools, hospitals, and shopping centres.
* Residential Zone: This division provides residential properties to the people working in GIFT City. It is designed to provide a world-class living environment to the residents.
* Transit-Oriented Development (TOD): This division is designed to promote sustainable transportation and connectivity in GIFT City. It includes a network of roads, pedestrian walkways, and cycle tracks.
The state level approval has been received for both the airport link and the internal extension at GIFT City and are now awaiting the Centre's nod. The [[Gujarat Metro Rail Corporation Limited|metro]] extension inside GIFT City will cover around 7km. It will be linked to the current [[Gujarat National Law University|GNLU]]-GIFT City metro line.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-04-29 |title=Ahmedabad-Gandhinagar Metro to touch down at airport, extend into GIFT City |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/ahmedabad-gandhinagar-metro-to-touch-down-at-airport-extend-into-gift-city/articleshow/120706533.cms |access-date=2025-12-03 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

Protection of Interest in Aircraft Objects Bill passed in Parliament this year which granted legal authority to the Cape Town Convention in India<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-02 |title='India presents excellent investment opportunity': PM Modi praises domestic carriers at IATA |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/india-news/india-presents-excellent-investment-opportunity-pm-modi-praises-domestic-carriers-at-iata/3865944/ |access-date=2025-12-03 |website=The Financial Express |language=en}}</ref>. [[Narendra Modi|Modi]] noted during his address that the new Act opens fresh opportunities for global aircraft [[Lease|leasing]] companies in India. He also pointed to the [[incentive]]s offered at Gift City, stating that these measures have made India an attractive destination for aircraft leasing.

== Tax benefits ==
GIFT City, through its International Financial Services Centre (IFSC), provides several tax benefits aimed at luring both domestic and international investments.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-08-29 |title=GIFT City explained: History & tax incentives of India's first 'Smart City' |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/gift-city-explained-history-tax-incentives-of-indias-first-smart-city/article65736969.ece |access-date=2023-06-20 |issn=0971-751X |archive-date=18 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230518082815/https://www.thehindu.com/business/gift-city-explained-history-tax-incentives-of-indias-first-smart-city/article65736969.ece |url-status=live }}</ref> These incentives include exemptions from certain taxes for companies under the new tax regime, tax holidays for specific sectors, and GST-free services for IFSC SEZ units. Further perks include various state subsidies and tax exemptions for exchanges established under the IFSC.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-16 |title=Tax Benefits for GIFT City: Unlocking India's Financial Potential |url=https://ashaval.com/tax-benefits-for-gift-city/ |access-date=2023-06-20 |language=en-US |archive-date=20 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230620101053/https://ashaval.com/tax-benefits-for-gift-city/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-27 |title=GIFT City: A Game-changer for Indian Startup Ecosystem |url=https://razorpay.com/blog/business-banking/gift-city-a-game-changer-for-indian-startup-ecosystem/ |access-date=2023-06-20 |language=en-US |archive-date=20 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230620095552/https://razorpay.com/blog/business-banking/gift-city-a-game-changer-for-indian-startup-ecosystem/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Liquor Policy in GIFT City ==
In December 2023, the Government of [[Gujarat]] authorized the controlled consumption of liquor within [[Gujarat International Finance Tec-City]] (GIFT City). This policy permits liquor to be served in restaurants, hotels, and clubs within GIFT City, but only to its permanent employees and their authorized visitors, as sanctioned by the respective companies' human resources departments. The sale of liquor bottles remains prohibited.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-12-26 |title=Liquor allowed in Gujarat's GIFT City, but is this the only game changer it needs? |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india-today-insight/story/liquor-allowed-in-gujarats-gift-city-but-is-this-the-only-game-changer-it-needs-2479700-2023-12-26 |accessdate=2023-12-26 |publisher=India Today}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Opinion: Gujarat Hub Turns "Ghost Town" After Work Hours. Solution: Liquor |url=https://www.ndtv.com/opinion/opinion-gujarat-hub-turns-ghost-town-after-work-hours-solution-liquor-4732449 |access-date=2023-12-26 |website=NDTV.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=www.ETRetail.com |title=Liquor in GIFT City: Industry leaders hail Gujarat govt's move as progressive, bold – ET Retail |url=https://retail.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/food-entertainment/grocery/liquor-in-gift-city-industry-leaders-hail-gujarat-govts-move-as-progressive-bold/106245926 |access-date=2023-12-26 |website=ETRetail.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Administration ==
=== Gujarat International Finance Tec-City Company Limited ===
The Government of Gujarat formed "Gujarat International Finance Tec-City Company Limited" (GIFTCL) to develop and implement GIFT City through its venture Gujarat Urban Development Company Limited (GUDCL). GIFT City is an {{convert|886|acre|adj=on|order=flip}} integrated project<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-25 |title=How Big Is GIFT City? A Simple Breakdown of India's New Financial Hub – MostlyNRI |url=https://mostlynri.com/how-big-is-gift-city/ |access-date=2025-12-03 |language=en-US}}</ref> that creates 62 million square feet of built-up area, including 67% commercial space, 22% residential space and 11% community space.

=== GIFT Managing Bodies ===
For the purpose of implementation of the SEZ, GIFT Company Limited has set up an SPV (Special Purpose Vehicle) (100% subsidiary of GIFTCL) namely GIFT SEZ Ltd, designated as the developer organization of the SEZ. GIFTCL has also set up 5 subsidiary companies for the implementation of specialized infrastructure including Power, Water, ICT (Information & Communication Technology), District Cooling and solid waste management.<ref name=":11"/>
* Gift Power Company Limited
* Gift Waste Management Services Limited
* Gift Water Infrastructure Limited
* Gift ICT Services Limited
* Gift Collective Investment Management Company Limited
* Gift SEZ Limited

extract:
Gujarat International Finance Tec-City also called GIFT City, is a central business district under construction in the Gandhinagar district as a suburb city of Gandhinagar-Ahmedabad Metropolitan Region in Gujarat, India. It is India's first operational greenfield smart city and international financial services centre, which the Government of Gujarat promoted as a greenfield project. In 2020 GIFT IFSC bagged 10th place in Finance Industry and top rank in emerging financial centres in the Global Financial Centres Index. In 2025, GIFT City secured the top rank in reputational advantage, ranked 40th in fintech, and achieved an overall ranking of 46th in the Global Financial Centres Index (GFCI 37).
The city is located on the banks of the Sabarmati River and is around 12 km (7.5 mi) from Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport. The city is designed so residents can walk to work, and includes commercial, financial and residential complexes. The city is connected through 4–6 lane state and national highways. The area is also served by the GIFT City metro station, connecting GIFT City to the Ahmedabad Metro network. The total area for the development of GIFT is 359 hectares (886 acres) out of which the special economic zone (SEZ) constitutes 106 hectares (261 acres). The project area under development can hence be classified under the SEZ area and the non-SEZ area (also known as the Domestic tariff area or the DTA).
Leadership at GIFT City has also evolved with its expansion. In July 2025, Sanjay Kaul was appointed as the new managing director and Group CEO.
During the meeting with top management of HSBC Plc, FM Nirmala Sitharaman outlined the roadmap towards Viksit Bharat, towards Atmanirbhar Bharat, sustainability, innovation, adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and inclusivity. GIFT IFSC, international financial services centre, is in Gandhinagar Gujarat.
The AI Centre of Excellence at GIFT City is aimed at creating a unified platform that brings together solution developers, experts, professionals, and start-ups under one roof, said Shri Bhupendra Patel at the time of the launch of Infosys Development Centre at GIFT City.
Several multinational banks including JP Morgan, Standard Chartered, Deutsche Bank, Citibank, HSBC. Barclays Bank, Bank of America, DFCC Bank, Qatar National Bank have set up IFSC Banking Units here.  Furthermore, it includes 35 fintech entities, two international stock exchanges with average daily trading volumes of $30.6 billion, as well as India's first international bullion exchange with 75 onboarded jewellers. With the opening of the first campuses of two Australian universities on 7 November 2023 in the presence of Indian counterpart Dharmendra Pradhan and Australian Education Minister Jason Clare, GIFT City is beginning to establish itself as the centre of foreign universities in the nation.
